text:
sara: Quick design poke — I'm proposing we adopt a "cleanroom" serializer boundary for safetensors-based checkpoints. The idea: a tiny, well-specified header that only carries a compat-signal + optional negotiation token. Keeps the runtime loader simple and lets format adapters live in a separate package. Thoughts?

li: I like the separation. How do you envision the compat-signal working? numeric version? feature-bitset?

sara: feature-bitset felt flexible, e.g. bits for: sharding, sparse-index, quant-metadata, signed-chunk. But we should keep the header <= 64 bytes to avoid perf/regression surprises.

matt: Can we sketch a minimal header example? That helps ops/instrumentation.

sara: Sure — rough sketch: ```
0x52 0x44 0x4F 0x57  // 'RDOW' magic
0x01               // header version
0x05               // feature bitset: sharding + signed-chunk
0x00 0x00 0x00 0x10 // negotiation token (optional, 4 bytes)
```

jonah: Two operational concerns: 1) negotiation roundtrip cost if we require token exchange; 2) how loaders fallback when a requested feature bit isn't supported.

li: For 1) we can keep negotiation optional. If token present, loader may attempt server-side resolution (useful for private deployments). If absent, loader uses local static policy.

matt: For 2) fallback order proposal: first try index-aware fast-path, then fall back to stream-demux sidecar, then to "indexless streaming" (single-file polyfill). Each step logs a clear telemetry tag.

rebecca: We should standardize the telemetry tag values now to avoid churn. e.g. `loader.fallback=index_first|sidecar|indexless` and `loader.compat=missing:<bitmask>`

ops-bot: Deploy note — any header change is backwards-impacting for Dedicated images. Recommend a thin compat shim that treats unknown header bits as opt-in features (i.e., fail closed only for bits that are explicitly security-sensitive).

sara: Good call. Operational policy: unknown bits => treat as unsupported but non-fatal unless it's the "signed-chunk" bit AND the runtime policy requires signature verification. That allows gradual rollout of signing.

jonah: Implementation detail: expose a small public API in the loader package: `probe_header(path) -> {features, token}` and `open_with_policy(path, policy)`. Keep probe fast and side-effect free.

li: Agree — also add a sticky cache of probe results keyed by content-hash so we avoid repeated probes for the same bundle across requests.

matt: One more: we need a migration plan for existing safetensors bundles. Suggest we accept current files (empty token, feature=0) and ship a conversion tool that can add headers in-place or produce sidecar metadata. Document both.

sara: Draft rollout: 1) land serializer boundary and probe API behind feature-flag; 2) deploy loader shim that accepts old and new headers; 3) run conversion tool on canary models; 4) enable stricter verification on canary hosts; 5) wide enable.

rebecca: Can we add a quick telemetry spike to measure extra bytes read by the probe on live traffic? Put the metric `loader.probe.read_bytes` and a histogram.

sara: Yep — I'll add that to the PR.

li: ACK. I'll follow up with a tiny RFC doc and include header binary layout + shim semantics.

matt: If nobody objects, I'll draft the loader API and the conversion tool skeleton next week.

sara: Thanks all. Short action items: li -> RFC draft; matt -> loader API PR; rebecca -> telemetry tags + dashboards; jonah -> list of security-sensitive bits.

li: tagging @safety to review the signed-chunk semantics later. :eyes:
